# TyraX game project

This is a **PlayStation 2 game project generated by the TyraX editor**. The
editor owns the data model (`<name>.tyra` + `objects/*.json`) and regenerates
the game's C++ sources from it; the game is built with the native
PS2DEV/OpenVCL toolchain and runs in PCSX2 (or on a real PS2 over the network).
Docker remains an optional fallback.

Detailed guides live in `.claude/skills/`:

- **tyra-project** — how the project is structured, which files are editor-owned
  vs yours, and the editor's headless CLI (inspect/build/modify without the GUI).
- **tyra-flowgraph** — flow graphs (the visual logic scripts): JSON format, node
  catalog, reading/writing graphs from the command line, AI generation.
- **tyra-scripting** — custom C++ scripts, custom flow nodes (`.flownode`),
  custom screen effects (`.screenfx`), and the VS Code extension.
- **tyra-menustyle** — the menu stylesheets (`menu-styles/*.menustyle`): what a
  sheet can say about how a menu LOOKS, what each thing costs on the console,
  and what is deliberately impossible.
- **tyra-building** — building, running in PCSX2, reading logs, debugging
  crashes and `TYRA_ASSERT` dumps.
- **tyra-vu-programs** — writing the microprogram VU1 runs over every vertex, in
  C++ (`src/vu/*.cpp`): slots, material classes, per-mesh parameters, the
  micro-memory budget, and the traps that only appear on the console.
- **tyra-vu0-kernels** — VU0 compute kernels (`src/vu0/*.cpp`): batching
  quadwords through the other vector unit and reading the answers back on the
  CPU.

The guides cite editor documentation as `docs/<page>.md`. Those pages are not
in this project; they are built into the editor. To read one, run
`"{TYRAX_EXE}" --search-docs "<terms>" [<page>]`, where `<page>` is the file
name without `.md`.

## The three rules that prevent lost work

1. **Never edit editor-owned files** - they are rewritten from the project data
   on every build/refresh and your changes are silently lost: everything under
   `src/gen/` and `vugen/`, every `*.gen.cpp` / `*.gen.hpp`,
   `inc/scene_data.hpp`, `inc/terrain_config.hpp` (all with the first line
   `Generated by TyraX. Do not edit - regenerated on every build.`), plus
   `src/main.cpp`, `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml` and
   `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json`, which carry no marker line but are
   rewritten all the same. Change the source data in the editor (or via the
   CLI) instead. Build flags go in the project preferences (`cppStandard`,
   `extraCompilerFlags`, `extraLinkerFlags`) or in a `user.mk` beside the
   Makefile, which is yours and which the Makefile includes last.
2. Files whose first line says `Generated by TyraX. Delete this line to take
   ownership of this file.` (`src/terrain_game.cpp`, `inc/terrain_game.hpp`,
   `inc/controls.hpp`, `inc/scripts/script.hpp`, `inc/scripts/flow_nodes.hpp`)
   are regenerated **only while that marker line is intact**. Delete the marker
   line first if you want to hand-edit them - and know that they then stop
   receiving editor updates.
3. Scene/game data lives in `<name>.tyra` and `objects/<id>.json`, not in the
   C++ sources. To change objects, preferences or graphs, edit those (the
   editor CLI validates and round-trips them) and the C++ regenerates.
